properties.statement: A FORCE-PUSHED REBASE ON AN OPEN PR RAN NO CI, AND THE PR WENT ON REPORTING ITSELF READY TO MERGE. Found here 2026-08-08 while landing the storyflow HEAL stack. PR #105 was rebased onto main after #106 squash-merged, and force-pushed. `gh run list --branch` showed ONE run, against the PRE-REBASE sha `5d097f9`; the rebased commit `16d6e11` had none and never got one. Meanwhile `gh pr view 105` reported `mergeable: MERGEABLE, mergeStateStatus: CLEAN` and `gh pr checks` reported nothing at all rather than reporting an absence. A reader doing the normal thing — checking the PR is clean before merging — would have merged a commit no gate had ever seen. THIS IS THE HOUSE FAILURE SHAPE, in the house's own words: a green that belongs to something other than what you are about to ship. Same family as BL-206 (`reflow2_check` reported OK over 20 artifacts it never swept), `dec:no-design-here-never-looked` ('no design here' asserted without looking), and `loop_status` reporting `unsurfaced_gaps: 0` before detect_gaps has ever run. Here the green was real — it just belonged to a different commit. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` triggers on `push: branches: [main]` and an unfiltered `pull_request:`, so nothing in the configuration explains the miss; GitHub simply did not raise a `synchronize` for that force-push. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED, and saying so matters: the retarget from a feature-branch base to `main` happened seconds after the push, and either the race or the base change may be responsible. NOT TESTED. WORKAROUND THAT WORKED, one command pair: `gh pr close 105 && gh pr reopen 105` fires `pull_request: reopened`, which is in the default trigger types, and CI queued immediately against the correct sha. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS PR: reflow2's own release procedure and [[branch-then-pr-practice]] both rest on 'mark ready only on green', and this is a case where green is present, current-looking, and about a commit that no longer exists in the branch. The check a human can actually perform is `gh run list --branch <b>` and compare `headSha` against `gh pr view --json headRefOid` — two commands, and neither is in any documented routine here. FIX SHAPE: add that comparison to the pre-merge routine in AGENTS.md / the release procedure; or have the gate itself refuse when the head sha has no completed run, which is the stronger form because it does not depend on remembering.
